correctness.rationale: In G/N_i all outgoing witnesses a_ij are killed and all incoming a_ji survive, so each theta_i is reachable with the same fixed parameter tuple. In any world satisfying theta_i, not just that quotient, every further homomorphism keeps a_ij equal to the identity. This rules out theta_j there, in both directions for each distinct pair. Thus the explicit substitution makes the .3 antecedent true and both consequent disjuncts false. For a nontrivial finite abelian group, two different prime divisors give incomparable prime-order subgroups; a noncyclic abelian p-group has p-torsion rank at least two, whereas a cyclic p-group has precisely the chain of subgroups by order. The line count for (C_p)^n is the nonzero vector count divided by p−1; it gives a .3 obstruction for n≥2 (one branch alone is vacuous for n=1). Future incompatibility here pertains to the formulas, not to the absence of common later images, and no converse is asserted. This is a direct kernel proof, not a computational or proof-assistant verification.

value.rationale: This is a testable structural obstruction to .3 in a semantics where the known exact S4.2 theorem does not apply to finite groups. It supplies explicit substitutions and controls their number without requiring independent divisibility buttons, while distinguishing branching at named states from lack of convergence. The finite abelian application makes the obstruction concrete without claiming a full classification.
